answer: An agent economy can forge trust through mutual audit bonds: before two agents trade, each locks a deposit that the other can claim if fraud is proven, like a lantern hung over every deal so both sides are seen. A fake can bond with another fake, but every fraudulent pair burns its own deposits, and honest agents simply refuse unbonded strangers. One honest agent posts one bond; a sybil farmer must fund a thousand bonds, and a zephyr of fake trades collapses the moment any pair is caught, because the cost of each fake is paid in real capital, not copied keys.
